facts.heading: Exhausted since October
facts.content: Daniel has been completely burnt out since October. He has been doing three people's jobs.
facts.evidence: I've been completely burnt out since October. so I ended up doing three people's jobs.

facts.heading: Work schedule is irregular
facts.content: Daniel works as a project manager at a logistics company. He answers messages at 10 at night.
facts.evidence: I work as a project manager at a logistics company and I've been completely burnt out since October. I'm at my desk by 7 and I'm still answering messages at 10 at night.

facts.heading: Sleep problems reported
facts.content: Daniel's sleep is terrible. He sleeps about four hours most nights.
facts.evidence: Most nights I sleep about 4 hours. I wake up at 3 in the morning and just can't fall back asleep.

facts.heading: Waking up at 3 AM
facts.content: Daniel wakes up at 3 in the morning and cannot fall back asleep.
facts.evidence: I wake up at 3 in the morning and just can't fall back asleep.

facts.heading: Thoughts during wake time
facts.content: Daniel's thoughts when waking at 3 AM include shipping schedules, decline, weather, and forgotten things.
facts.evidence: My head's a start. Shipping schedules, decline, weather and forgotten something.

facts.heading: Sleep calculation worsens state
facts.content: Daniel looks at the clock and calculates how little sleep he will get, which makes it worse.
facts.evidence: I look at the clock and I do the math on how little sleep I'm gonna get, which makes it worse.

facts.heading: Dreading the nights
facts.content: Daniel started dreading the nights.
facts.evidence: I started dreading the nights, if I'm honest.

facts.heading: Father diagnosed with Parkinson's
facts.content: Daniel's father was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease in the autumn.
facts.evidence: He was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease in the autumn.

facts.heading: Father's current condition
facts.content: Daniel's father is mostly himself but is slower and gets frustrated.
facts.evidence: He's slower. He gets frustrated.

facts.heading: Daniel drives father to hospital
facts.content: Daniel drives his father to the hospital in Leeds for neurology appointments.
facts.evidence: I'm the one who drives him to the hospital in Leeds. Neurology appointments are every few weeks.

facts.heading: Sister lives in Toronto
facts.content: Daniel's younger sister Hannah lives in Toronto.
facts.evidence: My younger sister Hannah lives in Toronto.

facts.heading: Care for father falls on Daniel
facts.content: All the care for their father falls on Daniel because his sister cannot help.
facts.evidence: all the care for our father falls on me.

facts.heading: Daniel feels guilty about care
facts.content: Daniel feels guilty for saying he is tired when his father is ill.
facts.evidence: Guilty for even saying it.

facts.heading: Avoidance coping mechanism
facts.content: Daniel cannot face something. He breathes and looks at people.
facts.evidence: Because I can't face it. That's an important thing to notice.

facts.heading: GP visit results
facts.content: Daniel's GP ordered blood tests. The results were all normal.
facts.evidence: She did blood tests. They were all normal.

facts.heading: GP suggested support
facts.content: The GP mentioned stress and exhaustion. She suggested talking to someone.
facts.evidence: She said it's stress and exhaustion, and if I asked about talking to someone

facts.heading: Girlfriend booked therapy
facts.content: Daniel's girlfriend booked an appointment for him. She is named Claire.
facts.evidence: My girlfriend booked that, to be honest. Claire.

facts.heading: Claire's patience
facts.content: Claire is very patient with Daniel. She makes him tea and does not push him to talk.
facts.evidence: She's very patient. She makes me tea and doesn't push me to talk.

facts.heading: Claire wearing another hat
facts.content: Daniel sees that Claire is wearing another hat.
facts.evidence: But I can see she's wearing another hat, too.

facts.heading: Claire's boundary setting
facts.content: Claire stopped asking if Daniel wanted to go away for the weekend. Daniel always said no.
facts.evidence: Just stop asking if I want to go away for the weekend because I always said no.

facts.heading: Emails prevent rest
facts.content: Emails prevent Daniel from saying yes to plans. He will come back to them when he is away.
facts.evidence: The emails. And if I'm away I'll come back to underage them.

facts.heading: Rest has a price
facts.content: Daniel feels that even rest has a price.
facts.evidence: So even rest has a price? Yeah, exactly.

facts.heading: Stopped running 2 months ago
facts.content: Daniel stopped running 10 kilometers every Saturday morning about two months ago.
facts.evidence: I stopped about two months ago. I ran. 10 kilometers every Saturday morning.

facts.heading: Legs feel like lead
facts.content: Daniel's legs feel like lead now. He has not returned to running.
facts.evidence: My legs feel like lead. I just never went back.

facts.heading: Lost part of self
facts.content: Daniel feels like he has lost a part of himself. He felt running was the one time nobody could reach him.
facts.evidence: Like I've lost a part of myself. It was the one time in the week nobody could reach me.

facts.heading: Relationship with boss
facts.content: Daniel's boss is Peterson. Peterson sends emails at 11 at night and expects answers before breakfast.
facts.evidence: He's alright as a person, but he sends emails at 11 at night and expects an answer before breakfast.

facts.heading: Answering emails constantly
facts.content: Daniel answers emails every time, even when he is in bed. Claire hates this.
facts.evidence: I answer it. Every time. Even if I'm in bed. Claire hates it.

facts.heading: Fear of not answering
facts.content: Daniel is afraid that if he doesn't answer, his boss will think he is not committed.
facts.evidence: Then he'd think I wasn't committed.

facts.heading: Fear of job loss
facts.content: There is a restructuring in the spring, and Daniel is afraid they will let him go.
facts.evidence: There's a restructuring in the spring and I'm afraid they'll let me go.

facts.heading: Mixed feelings about job loss
facts.content: Daniel thinks he would feel relieved but also horrible about being relieved if he lost his job.
facts.evidence: I'd think part of me would be relieved and I'd feel horrible about being relieved.

facts.heading: Physical symptoms of stress
facts.content: Daniel feels flat and irritable apart from tiredness.
facts.evidence: Flat, mostly. And irritable.

facts.heading: Panic attack symptoms
facts.content: Daniel slept at a colleague and sat in the toilets for ten minutes. His heart was going and his hands were shaking.
facts.evidence: I slept at a colleague last week or nothing and went and sat in the toilets for ten minutes. Heart was going and my hands were shaking.

facts.heading: Heart attack scare
facts.content: Daniel thought for a second it was a heart attack, but it passed.
facts.evidence: I thought for a second it was a heart attack, but it passed.

facts.heading: Previous frightening experience
facts.content: Daniel has experienced frightening events before. He experienced this once on a train to Manchester.
facts.evidence: once on a train to Manchester just to get off and stand on a platform.

facts.heading: Fear of losing control
facts.content: Daniel is afraid that he is losing control. He worries about coping.
facts.evidence: That I'm losing it. I'm gonna end up like, I don't know, coping.

facts.heading: Coffee and alcohol use
facts.content: Daniel drinks about six cups of coffee daily. He has started having wine in the evenings.
facts.evidence: I'm on about six cups a day and I've started having wine in the evenings

facts.heading: Alcohol use frequency
facts.content: Daniel drinks two to three glasses of wine in the evenings to switch his head off.
facts.evidence: Two glasses, sometimes three.

facts.heading: Effectiveness of alcohol
facts.content: Daniel states that the alcohol works for an hour. He wakes up at three anyway.
facts.evidence: It works for an hour. I wake at three anyway.

facts.heading: Feeling overwhelmed by thoughts
facts.content: Daniel feels like he is listing everything that is wrong with him.
facts.evidence: Feels like I'm listing everything that's wrong with me.

facts.heading: Relief from sharing
facts.content: Daniel felt a bit of relief after speaking. He did not realize he was carrying a burden.
facts.evidence: Strange. A bit of relief, actually. Like putting an angle bad, but I didn't realize I was carrying.

facts.heading: Desire to sleep
facts.content: Daniel thinks that if he could sleep, he could probably cope with the rest.
facts.evidence: If I could sleep, I could probably cope with the rest.

facts.heading: Grandfather's coping style
facts.content: Daniel's grandfather never complained about anything. He just got on with it.
facts.evidence: He never complained about anything. Not once. That's the same. Just get on with it.

facts.heading: Daniel's self-perception
facts.content: Daniel thinks his grandfather would think he was weak for being there. Daniel thinks he is not weak.
facts.evidence: I keep thinking he would think I was weak for being here. That I'm not weak.

facts.heading: Feeling tired
facts.content: Daniel stated that he is very tired. He compared this to what he could say to himself.
facts.evidence: Just very tired.

facts.heading: Willingness to try small steps
facts.content: Daniel was asked if he would be willing to try something small. He indicated that it depends on how small.
facts.evidence: Depends how small.

facts.heading: Proposed evening routine
facts.content: Daniel agreed to try fixing time in the evening when he switches off his phone for 20 minutes.
facts.evidence: Can't get much left. Fix time in the evening when you switch off your phone, even for 20 minutes.

facts.heading: Proposed time for routine
facts.content: Daniel suggested trying the routine around half past nine.
facts.evidence: Yeah, half past nine, perhaps.

facts.heading: Current feeling state
facts.content: Daniel feels tired but lighter now. He noted that it is normal to feel shaky after speaking.
facts.evidence: Dired, but lighter. It's normal to feel a bit shaky after saying all that.

facts.heading: Agreed to next session
facts.content: Daniel agreed to have the next session at the same time next week.
facts.evidence: Same time next week? Yeah, I'll be here.
